notes.question: JustVugg's question on #2264 (2026-10-22): DSV4_MM_WARP is on by default (auto) in PR #1's mm_batch, so it changes the prefill of every FP8 checkpoint on a generic CUDA build, not only the COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH=1 path the earlier manifests measured; measure the default configuration (no COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH) on the full V4 Flash, dev against the branch, prompt and decode, interleaved. It stays on by default if bit-identical and not slower. The point of this manifest is therefore 'not slower, bit-identical', not a speed-up: in the default configuration the prefill MoE runs on the CPU union in both arms, and the warp kernel only takes the batched attention's short fp8 rows.
notes.mm_warp_verify: Arm V (seq 8, not timed for a manifest: verify runs the old kernel beside the new one): B's configuration plus DSV4_MM_WARP_VERIFY=1 on the pr1 tip. serve.log counts 1500 mm_batch_w calls with 0 mismatching bits (last line 'mm-warp verify calls=1500 mismatches=0'); its texts are identical to A's. So the warp dense kernel that is on by default (auto: fp8 shapes with I a multiple of 256 and <= 1024) produced the old kernel's bits on every call it took in this configuration.
